title: The Prior Who Became a Moslem

keywords: the prior who became a moslem
full_text:
Upon the cool, cedar-crested heights of Mount Lebanon stood an ancient monastery celebrated throughout the Levant for the medicinal gardens of its venerable prior, Father Paul. The prior had spent forty years studying ancient manuscripts in Greek, Syriac, and Hebrew, tending to sick pilgrims of every faith who knocked upon the oak portal.

One autumn afternoon, a caravan of Muslim merchants traveling from Damascus to Beirut was caught in a furious blizzard on the mountain pass. Freezing and exhausted, fifty men and their animals sought refuge at the monastery gates.

Father Paul threw open the portals, welcomed the frozen travelers into the great stone refectory, built roaring fires of cedar logs, and shared his bread, cheese, and hot herb broths without inquiring into their creed.

Among the merchants was a venerable jurist of Baghdad, Shaykh Abdallah. As the storm raged for three days, the prior and the jurist sat by the hearth, engaging in deep and respectful dialogue on theology, the teachings of the prophets, the nature of divine mercy, and the universal moral duties of humankind.

Father Paul was profoundly moved by the moral clarity, philosophical depth, and spiritual universality of the Quranic teachings presented by the jurist. He realized that the essence of all divine revelation is one: to love the Creator, to act with righteous justice, and to serve humanity with compassionate charity.

When the storm cleared, Father Paul accompanied the caravan to Damascus, embraced the faith of Islam, and spent the remainder of his days teaching the harmony of the scriptures in the great Umayyad Academy, demonstrating that an open heart finds truth wherever its light shines.
moral: Sincere spiritual inquiry that seeks truth with an open heart discovers unity across all traditions.
